page.layout: One printed page of running commentary in one main column, with marginal reference notes ("Ver.15.", "Ver.20.") in the left margin. Running head at top centre and right. Catchword "Munere" at lower right. Right edge shows part of the neighbouring page, not transcribed.

main_text.p: Ver.15. [illegible, ~6 letters] Et juvencos decem.] Vulg. laris viginti. Vel legit, vel in animo habuit [illegible, ~3 letters] pro [illegible, ~3 letters]. Scitè Amama in Censurâ, Nobis de alieno non licèt esse tam benignis. LXX cum Hebraeo consentiunt, ταύρους δέκα. Similiter Chaldaeus, [illegible, ~4 letters] i.e. Et tauros decem.

Ver.20. [illegible, ~5 letters] Placabo iram ejus.] Ad verbum, operiam faciem ejus. Vel, ut Mercerus interpretatur, abstergam vultum ejus. Ità passim usurpari hoc verbum in sacrificiis asserit, q.d. detergere maculam & peccatum. Refert Ramban velle id significari esse magis Rabbinicum, & in Scripturâ deduci à [illegible, ~2 letters] lytro, quasi sacrificium pro redemptione animæ detur; ipse tamen priorem expositionem sequitur, ac notat, in Ezrâ [illegible, ~3 letters] esse pelves, ad abstergendo sanguine per sacerdotes ad labra eorum. Sic hoc in loco, velut abstergam ab irâ vultum ejus, i.e. placabo, & propitium mihi reddam, conciliabo. Aben Ezra hîc exponit [illegible, ~4 letters] per [illegible, ~3 letters], i.e. operiam & abscondam. Et [illegible, ~3 letters] per [illegible, ~3 letters], i.e. iram ejus. Ut 1 Sam.1.18. [illegible, ~6 letters] i.e. Et ira seu indignatio ejus (ad verb. & facies seu vultus ejus) non erat ei amplius. Facies pro irâ ponitur, quia ira in facie apparet, ibi statim se conspiciendam præbet. R.Salom.in eundem sensum interpretatur, [illegible, ~4 letters], i.e. indignationem ejus cessare faciam, seu auferam. Et citat illud Isai.28.18. ubi verbum [illegible, ~2 letters] sensu isto usurpatur, [illegible, ~6 letters], i.e. Et irritum erit fœdus vestrum cum morte. Chald. [illegible, ~3 letters] [illegible, ~3 letters], i.e. quiescere faciam indignationem ejus. Targum Jonath. [illegible, ~5 letters], i.e. reconciliabo affectum vultûs ejus.

page.notes: Hebrew and Greek words in the main text are largely illegible at this scan resolution and are marked accordingly. The right edge of the scan shows the neighbouring page and is not transcribed. Catchword at lower right read as "Munere".
